standard_prerequisites.name: The reduced base change of a finite compositum is a finite product of finite extensions and the corresponding map of integral closures is a product of the maps considered in the construction remark, hence surjective on spectra
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides a maximal ideal of the larger integral closure lying over a chosen prime of the smaller one, which is the point at which the comparison is made.

standard_prerequisites.name: Weak unramifiedness for a composite of extensions of discrete valuation rings implies weak unramifiedness of the intermediate extension, and the same holds for separability of the residue field extensions
standard_prerequisites.use: Yields assertion (1) by comparing the composite with its first factor.

standard_prerequisites.name: The equivalence between weak unramifiedness with separable residue extension and formal smoothness in the adic topology, which is the definition of a weak solution
standard_prerequisites.use: Translates the conclusion about weak unramifiedness and separable residue fields back into the statement about weak solutions.

core_obligations: Set up the reduced base changes of the three fraction fields and the integral closures of the two larger rings, and use the construction remark to see that the map between the integral closures is a finite product of the maps discussed there, in particular surjective on spectra (proof lines 34529-34538).

Choose a maximal ideal of the largest integral closure and consider the chain of discrete valuation rings obtained by localizing at the primes it meets below; record that the composite of the chain is the one whose properties are assumed or to be proved (proof lines 34538-34542).

For assertion (1), observe that if the composite is weakly unramified then so is the first factor, and if the residue field extension of the composite is separable then so is that of the subextension, so the formal smoothness criterion gives the conclusion (proof lines 34542-34549).

For assertion (2), repeat the same localization argument with the hypothesis that the first factor and each factor of the reduced base change are weak solutions, concluding that the composite is one, as the author states (proof lines 34549-34552).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a chain of localizations at a maximal ideal of the largest integral closure (proof lines 34529-34542).
Compare the three rings in that chain, showing that weak unramifiedness and separability pass down to the intermediate extension (proof lines 34542-34549).
Translate the conclusion back to weak solutions and repeat the argument for the compositional statement (proof lines 34547-34552).
difficulty_reason: The statement concerns a tower of three extensions of discrete valuation rings and a finite extension of the bottom fraction field, and says that being a (weak) solution descends to the intermediate extension and composes from the intermediate extension to the top when the reduced base change is a product of fields that are themselves (weak) solutions (statement lines 34516-34527). The proof takes the reduced base changes and the corresponding integral closures, observes through the construction remark that the map between the closures is a finite product of the standard maps and hence surjective on spectra, chooses a maximal ideal and reduces to a chain of three discrete valuation rings, where weak unramifiedness and separability of residue extensions visibly pass to the intermediate extension (proof lines 34529-34552). The reduction to a single chain of localizations is the device that makes both assertions follow from elementary properties of the composite.
